title: FUEL LEAK

alert.trigger: FOB + FU significantly less than FOB at engine start or decreasing; fuel spray seen from an engine, pylon or wingtip/sharklet; total fuel decreasing abnormally; a developing imbalance; a tank decreasing too fast; excessive fuel flow with low N1; fuel smell in the cabin; destination EFOB amber or "DEST EFOB BELOW MIN"; depending on the FWC standard, the FUEL F.USED/FOB DISAGREE alert.

effectivity.note: The center tank lines differ: CTR TK PUMP 1 and 2 on HS-TXA..TXO, CTR TK L and R XFR on HS-TXP..TXU.

summary: When a leak is confirmed: amber LAND ASAP. If the leak is confirmed from an engine or pylon, shut that engine down and do not restart it. If not, keep the crossfeed closed, stop the center tank feed and watch the inner tanks. One tank depleting faster by at least 300 kg in less than 30 min: shut down that engine to tell an engine leak from a wing leak. Both depleting alike: suspect the center tank or APU feed line. Do not use the reversers for landing.

Consider a fuel leak for any message or alert on fuel quantity or imbalance
Depending on the FWC standard, the FUEL F.USED/FOB DISAGREE alert may address both cases of fuel leak and fuel over read

tables.caption: FCTM table of indications and observations.
rows: Fuel spray from an engine/pylon. For one engine side only: excessive fuel flow or significant N1 decrease. One wing tank decreases abnormally fast.
Fuel spray from the wing. One wing decreases abnormally fast.

background.text: A fuel leak may be detected if the FOB + FU is significantly less than the FOB at engine start or decreasing, a passenger observes fuel spray, the total fuel decreases at an abnormal rate, an imbalance develops, a tank decreases too fast, fuel flow is excessive with low N1, fuel is smelt in the cabin, or the destination EFOB turns amber or "DEST EFOB BELOW MIN" appears.
On HS-TXP..TXU a tank overflowing (pipe rupture in a tank) is also listed as a way to detect a leak.
APU OFF for a fuel smell in the cabin prevents additional fuel loss through the APU feeding line.

technique.text: If the leak is confirmed from the engine or pylon, the engine is shut down to stop the leak and to prevent a fire hazard from fuel leaking onto hot engine surfaces.

If it is not confirmed, each tank is isolated so each wing tank feeds its own engine. If one wing tank decreases faster, its engine is shut down to confirm whether the leak is from the wing tank or the engine.

The 300 kg threshold allows for fuel system accuracy. A leak rate that is constant or increasing below it indicates a permanent asymmetric leak developing over time, and should be considered a leak from a wing or an engine.
If both wing tanks decrease symmetrically and the center tank quantity decreases, the leak comes from the center tank or the APU feed line.

Do not use the reversers at landing even if available: their airflow blows leaking fuel toward the engine air inlet or the brakes, which may overheat the engine or start a fire, or reduce brake performance or start a fire on hot brakes.
If the crew detects a fuel leak before the ECAM alert is triggered, the crew can activate the QRH FUEL LEAK procedure.

related.title: ENG 1(2) SHUT DOWN
related.why: The QRH does not name it here. Apply it after the engine shutdown in this procedure, as confirmed by the user.
key_actions: See the ENG 1(2) FAIL brief, which holds this procedure

related.title: FUEL IMBALANCE
related.why: A fuel imbalance may indicate a leak; do not apply FUEL IMBALANCE if a leak is suspected.

related.title: ENG RELIGHT IN FLIGHT
related.why: ENGINE RESTART: CONSIDER if the leak continues after the engine shutdown (wing leak suspected).
key_actions: See the ENG RELIGHT IN FLIGHT brief

related.title: FUEL OVERREAD
related.why: The opposite indication: FOB + FU significantly more than the FOB at engine start, or increasing.
key_actions: Apply the QRH FUEL OVERREAD procedure

values.HS-TXP..TXU: CTR TK L and R XFR

differences.topic: After shutdown of the engine on the leaking side

values.HS-TXA..TXO: CTR TK PUMP 1 and 2 ON immediately
values.HS-TXP..TXU: CTR TK L and R XFR ON if the leak stops; CTR TK XFR (non-leaking side) ON if it continues

gaps.text: The QRH does not say which ECAM procedure follows the engine shutdown. The brief points to ENG 1(2) SHUT DOWN under Related procedures, confirmed by the user. HS-TO-only versions (QRH 21.06B, FCOM ENG 1(2) FUEL LEAK P 103/226) are excluded.
The FCTM mentions a FUEL F.USED/FOB DISAGREE alert "depending on the FWC standard". The HS-TX FCOM procedures do not list it. The brief shows it as a possible trigger, confirmed by the user.
"ENGINE MASTER 1 OFF" is the PDP example of the crosscheck wording: apply it to the engine concerned. The PDP has no fuel module; the flow is the standard QRH sequence.
The manuals print a separate version for each HS-TX group. "From the manuals" merges them into one procedure, with a chip on the lines that differ, confirmed by the user.
